reason: The cited evidence shows that Ti and Zn can form intermetallic phases that act as corrosion barriers (E1) and that non-equilibrium microstructures with segregations exist after SPS (E2), but no evidence supports the key mechanistic claims that thermal aging produces fine precipitates which nucleate protective oxides, or that such oxides improve both corrosion and oxidation behavior; E3 and E4 discuss pest oxidation and Sn effects in unrelated alloy systems.
premises: Thermal aging drives decomposition of metastable solid solution into fine intermetallic precipitates
Fine intermetallic precipitates act as nucleation sites for protective oxide scales
Protective oxide scales improve corrosion resistance and high-temperature oxidation behavior
Ti- and Zn-rich intermetallics can act as corrosion barriers
